prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1379; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured vehicle and third-party vehicle both sustained front-end damage. Insured reports no airbag deployment. Third-party driver reported neck pain at the scene and was transported by EMS for evaluation. Liability appears disputed pending police report review.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. Reporting officer notes both vehicles traveling at low speed, one vehicle crossed the centerline during an evasive maneuver. Preliminary fault assessment under review. Photos of both vehicles reviewed and consistent with the reported impact zone. Third-party claimant has retained counsel, who has requested all communications be routed through the firm.

Entry 3: Counsel submitted medical records indicating a diagnosis of concussion with post-concussive symptoms including headaches, light sensitivity and difficulty concentrating. Treating physician has restricted claimant from work for a limited period. Records requested for prior head or neck complaints to establish baseline. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury severity and anticipated treatment duration.

Entry 4: Independent medical review scheduled. Counsel has indicated claimant may require a neuropsychological evaluation. Requested itemized billing from treating providers and wage documentation from employer. Discussed with counsel the coverage position on liability and the status of the property damage claim. No settlement offer extended at this time.

Entry 5: Received updated treatment notes showing gradual improvement in symptoms, though claimant continues to report intermittent headaches. Independent medical examiner report pending. Liability determination remains under review. Diary set for follow-up with counsel once the medical review is complete and all outstanding records have been received.
